ing: coarse ground pork, or 4 ready-made smoked pork sausages
st: Rinse the sauerkraut briefly in a strainer and squeeze it dry.
Cook the bacon in a wide pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until the fat melts.
Add the sauerkraut, caraway and [[0.5 cup]] water. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
If using fresh pork, mix it with garlic, pepper and [[1 tsp]] salt and shape into thick links by hand.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Brown the sausages on all sides for about 15 minutes, turning often, until they reach 160°F (71°C) inside.
Pre-smoked sausages just need 8 minutes to heat through and brown.
Serve the sausages on the sauerkraut with mustard on the side.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes until tender. Drain and mash until smooth.
Fry the bacon and half the onion in a pan for 6 minutes. Mix into the mash with [[0.5 tsp]] pepper, marjoram and salt.
Mix [[2 cup]] flour, 1 egg, [[0.25 cup]] warm water and [[1 tsp]] salt, then knead for 5 minutes. Rest 20 minutes under a bowl.
Roll the dough very thin. Cut into 2-inch squares.
Put a small ball of filling on each square, fold into a triangle, and press the edges well. Bring the points together to form a little hat.
Boil the dumplings in salted water for 8 minutes until they float and stay tender.
Fry the remaining onion in [[3 tbsp]] butter for 5 minutes until golden.
Toss the dumplings in the butter and top with chives.

ing: ribs or ham hock, or smoked sausage
st: Drain the soaked beans and boil them in fresh water for 45 minutes until almost tender.
Add the smoked pork, [[8 cup]] total water if needed, and bay leaves. Simmer 15 minutes.
Add the sauerkraut and potatoes and simmer 20 more minutes until the potatoes are soft.
Fry the bacon in a small pan for 4 minutes. Stir in [[1 tbsp]] flour and the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir this mixture into the stew and simmer 5 minutes to thicken.
Remove the bones and shred any meat, then return it to the pot.
Season with [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and salt, then serve hot.
Drain the soaked beans. Put them in a pot with the smoked pork and [[9 cup]] water.
Boil, then simmer for 40 minutes.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the onion mix, barley, carrots, bay leaf and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper to the pot.
Simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the potatoes and cook 15 more minutes until everything is soft and the stew is thick.
Take out the bones, shred the meat, and return it to the pot. Season with salt.
Melt [[3 tbsp]] lard in a heavy pot and cook the onions for 10 minutes until golden.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in [[3 tbsp]] paprika so it does not burn.
Return to low heat, add the meat, garlic, caraway, bay leaves and [[2 tsp]] salt. Stir to coat.
Add [[2 cup]] water, cover, and simmer for 60 minutes.
Stir in the peppers and tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes and [[2 cup]] more water. Simmer 30 minutes until potatoes and meat are tender. Pork should read 145°F (63°C) at least.
Season to taste and serve in bowls with bread.
Mix [[2.5 cup]] flour, 1 egg, [[0.5 cup]] warm water, [[1 tbsp]] oil and [[1 tsp]] salt into a dough. Knead 8 minutes and rest 30 minutes.
Mix the cottage cheese, 2 eggs, [[0.5 cup]] sour cream, chives and a pinch of salt for the filling.
Roll the dough into a very thin rectangle on a floured cloth.
Brush with [[2 tbsp]] melted butter and spread the filling over it, leaving an inch on the edges.
Roll up like a jelly roll using the cloth. Wrap tightly in the cloth and tie the ends.
Simmer in salted water for 30 minutes. Drain and unwrap.
Toast the breadcrumbs in [[4 tbsp]] butter until golden, 4 minutes.
Slice the roll, top with the crumbs, and serve with the remaining sour cream.

ing: for the dough and filling: divided
st: Mix the yeast with [[1 cup]] warm milk and [[2 tbsp]] sugar. Wait 8 minutes until foamy.
Add [[4 cup]] flour, [[0.25 cup]] melted butter, 1 egg, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, and knead 8 minutes into a soft dough.
Cover and let it rise 1 hour until doubled.
Mix [[3 cup]] ground walnuts, [[0.5 cup]] honey, [[0.5 cup]] hot cream, [[0.25 cup]] butter, [[1 tsp]] vanilla, [[1 tsp]] cinnamon and 1 egg into a spreadable filling.
Roll the dough very thin into a large rectangle.
Spread the filling evenly and roll up tightly like a jelly roll.
Fit the roll into a greased loaf pan or ring, seam down. Let it rest for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Bake 50 minutes until golden, covering with foil if browning too fast.
Cool fully before slicing.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Butter a 9x13 inch pan.
Mix the poppy seeds with [[0.25 cup]] sugar and the milk. Mix the walnuts with [[0.25 cup]] sugar. Mix the cottage cheese with 1 egg and [[0.25 cup]] sugar.
Toss the grated apples with the raisins and cinnamon.
Lay 3 sheets of phyllo in the pan, brushing each with melted butter.
Spread the poppy layer, add 2 sheets of phyllo, then spread the walnut layer. Repeat with the cheese, then the apple layer, brushing with butter between layers.
Finish with 3 sheets of phyllo on top.
Whisk 2 eggs with [[1 cup]] cream and pour over the top. Pour remaining butter over.
Bake 50 minutes until golden and set. Cool 20 minutes before cutting.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Bake the pastry sheets on lined trays, topped with another tray to keep them flat, for 20 minutes until golden. Cool.
Whisk the yolks, [[0.5 cup]] sugar, [[0.25 cup]] flour and [[0.25 cup]] cornstarch with a splash of cold milk until smooth.
Heat the remaining milk until steaming. Slowly pour it into the yolk mix while whisking.
Return to the pot and cook on medium heat, whisking, for 5 minutes until thick. Let it boil gently for 1 minute.
Stir in [[1 tsp]] vanilla and a pinch of salt. Cover the surface with plastic and chill 1 hour.
Whip [[1 cup]] cold cream with [[1 tsp]] vanilla to soft peaks.
Fold the whipped cream into the cold custard.
Put one pastry sheet in a square pan, spread the cream on top, and cover with the second sheet. Chill 30 minutes.
Cut with a serrated knife and dust with powdered sugar.
